messages.subject: Fwd:
parts:
Hi Everybody,
  The generative process:

  There are 2 entities (A,B)

entity-A recieves a number from B in the range (0, infinity) A draws a random number from a log-normal distribution with parameters val_mu and val_sigma . if the number that A draws is less than that which it recieved from B then A responds to B saying it had won and presents it with the number it drew otherwise A just responds to B saying it lost. Now B has no knowledge of parameters of the distribution (it knows the family not the parameters) . After performing several iterations it has the following data.

[(b0,a0) (b1,nil) (b2,a2) (b3,a3) (b4,nil) (b5,nil) .... ]

In the above list of pairs, the first-value of the pair tells you the value that B presented to A and the second-value of the pair tells you the value that it recieved on success or nil if it lost that iteration. 
 I know that we can come up with a strategy for values that B can present to A. However, to keep the problem simple let us assume B has some strategy (could be sub-optimal) to present A with values.
Now B has to infer the parameters of the log-normal distribution that A is using.

I am a newbie to probabilistic programming.. I have comeup with the forllowing formulation. I would love to hear any feedback.

As a first cut I decided to ignore the value I get when I win the iteration. Let us assume that the Q(b) be the cumulative distribution function of A's private probability distribution function f(b).

Then probability of seeing the observed data is 

Q(b0)*(1-Q(b1))*Q(b2)*Q(b3)*(1-Q(b4))*(1-Q(b5)) .... 

Now I can possibly take log of the above to get log-likelihood and then optimize the function to maximize the log-likelihood to obtain the parameters of A's private distribution.  My naive newton-raphson was numerically very unstable. Then I decided to use Stan. However I am having trouble expressing my problem.

I used the following stan code to generate data for the problem which worked fine.


data  {
  real val_mu;
  real bid_mu;
  real<lower=0> val_sd;
  real<lower=0> bid_sd;
}
parameters  {
  real<lower=10> bid;
  real<lower=0> val;
}
model  {
  val~lognormal(val_mu,val_sd);
  bid~lognormal(bid_mu,bid_sd);
}
generated quantities {
  int<lower=0,upper=1> win;
  if (val<bid) win<-1;
  else win<-0;
}

This code successfully generated the sample data.

Now my goal is to infer the parameters val_mu and val_sd from the data. The stan code I used is the following

data {
  int<lower=10> N;
  real<lower=0> bids[N];
  int<lower=0,upper=1> wins[N];
}
parameters {
  real val_mu;
  real<lower=0> val_sd;
}
model {
  real val;
  
  for(i in 1:N) {
  val_mu~cauchy(-15,4);
  val_sd~cauchy(0,10);  
  val~lognormal(val_mu,val_sd);
    if (val>bids[i]) wins[i]<-1; else wins[i]<-0;
  }
}

I was hoping I can infer val_mu and val_sd from the above stan code by providing N, bids and wins(0 for loss and 1 for a win) as generated by my previous stan code. However, it complains about the line
"if (val>bids) wins<-1; else wins<-0"

It says I can't assign in the model block. Which kind of makes-sense... How can I express the relationship that wins[i] is 1 when bids[i]>val? Can somebody help?
Thanks in advance. I looked through all the functions .. I am thinking the rank function could be helpful but still don't have a solution . I would greatly appreciate a hint in solving this problem.
Thanks,
Sunil.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users]
parts:
You want to take a look at the censoring chapter of the manual.

You can't assign to a parameter ever in Stan. You can assign
a value to a transformed parameter only in the transformed parameters
block.

Start by formulating what the data is going to look like. Do you
observe the draw from A and draw from B? The easiest way to do this
is to forget about the ordering (which doesn't matter as formulated)
and do this:

data {
int<lower=0> N_losses;
vector<lower=0>[N_losses] B_losses;
int<lower=0> N_wins;
vector[N_wins] A_wins;
}

I don't think you even need the n

This unfortunately doesn't express the constraint that A_wins[n] < B_wins[n],
so you have to make sure the data's OK from the outside. Then you are
trying to estimate two parameters of the lognormal:

parameters {
real mu;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}

And the model is just a censored observation model:

model {
for (n in 1:N_losses)
increment_log_prob(log(lognormal_ccdf(B_losses[n], mu, sigma)));
A_wins ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);
}

lognormal_ccdf(y, mu, sigma) = 1 - lognormal_cdf(y, mu, sigma)

so it's the probability that a value above y is drawn from lognormal(mu,sigma);

Then the wins just get drawn from the plain-old lognormal, because
the draw of A's number isn't conditioned on B's number.

- Bob
